name: Bays Mountain
summary: CCC-built 1937 tower in Bays Mountain Park, also called Garden Mountain or ET-12; climbable only on a capped Visit Kingsport hike (registration full when checked); height and county records disagree.
design: steel tower with a seven-foot-square lookout shelter (1953 account)
agency: Tennessee Division of Forestry operated it; City of Kingsport administers the site

access.note: Inside Bays Mountain Park. Visit Kingsport listed a capped early-arrival hike (12 places; registration full when checked) that includes going up inside the tower. No general climbing access found.

visit.trail_note: About 3.3 miles round trip on the Visit Kingsport early-arrival hike; the last stretch is steep with steps and switchbacks; the tower is not ADA compliant

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps (NHLR; Bays Mountain History)
George McCloud, towerman after six seasons (Kingsport News, 17 Nov 1948, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Brush blaze of about 10 acres at the foot of Bays Mountain, found by a state forester on patrol from the tower (Kingsport Times, 27 Oct 1953)
Govan Smith Jr. spent about five months a year in the shelter (Kingsport Times-News, 13 Dec 1953, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Kingsport News, 5 Oct 1955: state bought a dozen 80-foot steel towers and listed one for Sullivan County atop Bays Mountain; no source found that a tower went up on this ridge
Registered 24 March 2020 as US 1401, TN 37 as the Garden Mountain Fire Tower, nominated by Don Gouge
